div.head: Hn 48.1a
div.ab: Si quis enim a iusticia regis inplacitatus ad consilium exierit et ad inculpacionem non responderit, XX ma[n]ce uel ouerseunesse regis culpa sit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 571 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: marce Hss. Edd.; verbessert aus 37, 2; mͣ Sc
marce MSS edd.; corrected from 37, 2; mͣ Sc

Vgl. Gl Rechtsgang 14b—17f; Ducange s. v. consilium. Dem wegen Notzucht von Amts wegen Beklagten, der Rechtsbeistand erbittet, weigert diesen der Richter: iura non patiuntur, quod habeatis consilium contra regem, und schickt narratores fort (um 1300); Güterbock Stud. z. Engl. Strafproz. 29. 39—mancas uel auerseunes, dahinter über Linie -sum wohl statt -ssam—48, 1b aliquis{30}—48, 1c -ssit{23} Rs

Cf. Gl Rechtsgang 14b—17f; Ducange s. v. consilium. When a man accused of rape ex officio asks for legal counsel, the judge refuses it to him: iura non patiuntur, quod habeatis consilium contra regem, and sends the narratores away (c. 1300); Güterbock Stud. z. Engl. Strafproz. 29. 39—mancas uel auerseunes, followed above the line by -sum, probably for -ssam—48, 1b aliquis{30}—48, 1c -ssit{23} Rs

div.ab: For if anyone impleaded by the king's justice has gone out to take counsel and has not answered the charge, let him be liable for 20 mancuses or the king's overseunesse.
